bugs.headline: Netconf-yang RPC push for Cisco-IOS-XE-l2vpn fails due to the order of statements in XML
bugs.description: Symptom: RPC push fails due to the order of the XML under the following model: http://cisco.com/ns/yang/Cisco-IOS-XE-l2vpn The failure is dealing with EVPN. The order in which you add the XML configs is causing a pre-check dependency failure during the commit state. For instance, you may see something like this: application invalid-value error inconsistent value: Device refused one or more commandserror_cli evpn ethernet-segment 101 3 % Configure the Ethernet Segment first before associating interface to it evpn ethernet-segment 101 exit 0 evpn ethernet-segment 101 exit Other yang modules are able to handle this gracefully or re-order it before the commit state without causing an error. Conditions: The issue occurs because the XML lists a config (such as an interface config) that requires a global level configuration / definition to be declared before its applied. For instance, with the following RPC that deals with EVPN, the ES value on the interface appears before the globally defined ES value 2026-09-17 12:48:33 | DEBUG | ncclient.transport.ssh | [host ci1284 session-id 352] queueing 1/0/11 101 101 0 00.00.00.00.00.00.00.01.01 Due to the top to bottom approach with this particular yang module, it fails. Other yang models are able to handle the re-order of the XML more gracefully to avoid an error / failure. The netconf-yang standard suggests XML order shouldn't matter so this might cause unexpected results with the RPC push. Workaround: Option A: Use multiple operations (Sequential) Instead of pushing one large XML block, break the operation into two: RPC Push 1: Only send the global level l2vpn / evpn configuration. RPC Push 2: Send the interface-level ethernet-segment association. By separating them into two RPCs, you guarantee the global configuration exists before the interface attempts to reference it. Option B: Re-order the XML (If possible) While the NETCONF standard suggests XML order shouldn't matter, some Cisco YANG models are sensitive to the order of elements within the block. Try moving the block above the block in your XML. Further Problem Description:

bugs.headline: L2TPv2 multihop (LTS): data Ns stuck at 0 (S=1) on sequencing-enabled leg on ASR1001-HX, causing PPP/IPCP failure
bugs.description: Resolves PPP/IPCP negotiation failures in multihop L2TPv2 when data channel sequencing is used. Symptom: In an L2TPv2 multihop environment, PPP authentication or IPCP negotiation fails after the L2TP tunnel and session are established. The LTS sends data packets with S=1 but Ns stays at 0. Conditions: Observed on ASR1001-HX acting as an L2TP Tunnel Switch (LTS), when data channel sequencing is enabled on a session leg (by AVP-39 or by in-band detection). Seen in the 17.7 release train and later. Not seen in the 17.6 release train. Workaround: Disable L2TP data channel sequencing on BOTH the LAC and the LNS. Disabling it on only one side does not resolve the issue. Further Problem Description: When sequencing is enabled, the LTS sets S=1 in the L2TP data header of forwarded packets but does not increment Ns. The peer accepts only the first packet and does not respond to the following ones, so PPP negotiation does not complete.
